text:
Andreas Englund is on his sixth NHL team, and in Detroit he has found something like a steady job. NHL.com described him as providing a "sense of security" to the Red Wings' defense corps, and his minutes have grown to 14.6 a night over the last ten games, almost three more than before.

He plays the way his line shows: 48 hits in 16 games, very few shots. The goal at Florida on Nov. 12 was a rare one; Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom noted it was his first since October 2024. He had 2 goals in 200 NHL games before this season.

The numbers back up the depth role. Detroit has held 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, a little better than without him, and the goals have run slightly ahead of the chances. He played only 3 NHL games last season, so even this much stability is a step.

Nobody is asking him for offense. A third pair defenseman who keeps the shot share above even is worth keeping in the lineup, and so far that's what he has been.
